title: A chemically plausible route from simple feedstocks to evolving heredity

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a reproducible chemical system that starts with simple, geochemically defensible feedstocks and energy sources, produces information-bearing molecules, and carries them through repeated reproduction, heritable variation and selection. Its defining advance would be connecting these activities into a compatible experimental route, so that the products of chemical synthesis can become participants in an evolving molecular population. This is a proposed capability; the supplied evidence does not demonstrate the complete route.

RNA provides a concrete experimental approach because RNA molecules can carry sequence information and catalyze reactions. The reviewed 2024 work demonstrates an important part of this approach: an engineered RNA polymerase ribozyme enabled reproduction and evolution of a separate catalytic RNA. Connecting such molecular heredity to plausible nonliving starting materials would require substantially more than improving an isolated copying reaction.

Conceptual scope: the target is experimental feasibility under defensible chemical conditions. Establishing that a route actually operated on early Earth is a separate historical question requiring additional evidence. A successful experiment could reveal one possible origin of evolving heredity even if Earth's pathway used different molecules, environments or intermediate steps.

significance.text: Conditional significance: connecting plausible chemical production to sustained molecular heredity would demonstrate a route by which nonliving chemistry can acquire the capacity for cumulative evolution. The direct scientific consequence would be an experimentally tractable bridge between making molecules and maintaining functional information across generations. Describing that achievement as foundational is a scientific assessment of the proposed integration, rather than a ranking established by the supplied sources.

The 2024 RNA experiment illustrates why preserving information matters. Its higher-fidelity polymerase supported a succession of variants of the separate catalytic RNA with increasing fitness. An integrated feedstock-to-heredity system would extend this kind of result by connecting the supply and regeneration of molecular components to the evolutionary process itself.

Conditional downstream possibilities include testing how environmental cycles affect the emergence of heredity, comparing alternative chemical routes, and investigating which constraints permit molecular complexity to accumulate. The impact has important boundaries: evolving molecules would not by themselves establish cellular life, self-maintaining metabolism or unrestricted evolutionary complexity. Laboratory feasibility would also leave historical occurrence unresolved.

missing_breakthrough.text: Integration requirement: the missing capability is a compatible route linking feedstock chemistry, production of information-bearing polymers, copying, separation or release of copied strands, and repeated selection. Each stage must deliver usable material to the next under conditions the overall system can tolerate. The supplied evidence does not substantiate the full feedstock-formation chain or establish the present status of every approach to this integration; these remain requirements of the proposed innovation rather than a comprehensive finding about the field.

Replication fidelity is a documented barrier to a stronger form of autonomy. The 2024 study distinguishes evolution of a separate, smaller functional RNA from autonomous evolution of the polymerase that copies it. The authors identify further improvements in fidelity as necessary to maintain and evolve RNA enzymes as complex as the polymerase itself. Demonstrating evolution of a copied target therefore does not establish that the copying machinery can reproduce and evolve autonomously.

Replacing investigator-mediated regeneration is another concrete engineering challenge. The reviewed procedure used purification, reverse transcription, PCR and transcription to carry the evolving RNA through successive rounds. Those operations demonstrate how a laboratory can sustain the experiment, but they leave open how an integrated chemical system would recover usable products, regenerate its molecular population and continue selection without that biological machinery and repeated handling.

Engineering synthesis: a complete route would also need to reconcile component supply, energy input, molecular stability and copying conditions. It must distinguish productive reproduction from accumulation of unusable products, and heritable adaptation from enrichment caused solely by investigator choices. The supplied materials do not determine which chemical architecture could meet these requirements together.

current_state.text: In the study published on 4 March 2024, Papastavrou, Horning and Joyce demonstrated RNA-catalyzed evolution of a separate functional RNA, the hammerhead ribozyme. Eight rounds of evolution were conducted in parallel using two polymerases. The reviewed article reports maintenance of heritable information and progressively increasing fitness in the higher-fidelity lineage. This demonstrates reproduction and selection of a catalytic RNA with assistance from supplied copying machinery; it does not demonstrate autonomous evolution of the polymerase itself.

The scope of that demonstration includes substantial experimental intervention. Full-length products were purified by gel electrophoresis, and the procedure included reverse transcription, PCR and transcription to regenerate RNA. Consequently, the eight-round result does not establish continuous reproduction from simple geochemical feedstocks or independence from complex biological enzymes. The supplied review assessed the retained article text, but did not inspect linked supplementary materials or figure images.

The supplied research attributes a further result to Attwater and colleagues in a paper dated 28 May 2025: supplied trinucleotides and pH/freeze–thaw cycles reportedly enabled exponential RNA replication, including copying a fragment of an engineered polymerase ribozyme. It also states that the experiment did not generate that ribozyme and its substrates from simple geochemical feedstocks. These details remain unverified within the supplied evidence package: the retained PubMed artifact contains only a cookie-access message, which cannot establish the article's identity, experimental results or limits. The research's earlier statement that an abstract and figure descriptions were inspected is not substantiated by that retained artifact. This access limitation does not show that the reported result is false.

Evidence boundary: these materials establish a dated, partial demonstration of RNA heredity and evolution, while leaving the complete proposed route unestablished. The supplied search record is empty, so the package cannot determine the latest state of the field as of 1 November 2026. It also cannot establish that no other integrated approach has succeeded.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: begin with explicitly specified, geochemically defensible feedstocks and energy inputs, generate information-bearing polymers, and sustain repeated sequence-dependent reproduction and selection. The operational specification should identify all supplied components, environmental cycles and permitted interventions, including any initial catalyst or seed. It should show how continued reproduction proceeds without repeated investigator-supplied purification or complex biological enzymes. These are proposed criteria for this innovation, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Geochemical feedstocks yield polymers with sequence-dependent reproduction and selection

completion_criteria.text: Proposed evidence for heredity and evolution should connect sequence changes to inherited functional differences across successive generations. Controls should distinguish reproduction from persistence of the starting material and distinguish selection from transient enrichment or investigator-driven replacement. The experiment should document whether the copying machinery is merely supplied, replenished externally, reproduced by the system, or itself capable of evolution; these represent materially different levels of autonomy.
completion_criteria.label: Sequence changes confer inherited functional differences across successive generations

completion_criteria.text: The reviewed RNA study provides a concrete benchmark for interpreting such evidence: propagation and evolution of a functional target can be demonstrated while regeneration still depends on purification and enzyme-mediated laboratory steps. A convincing integrated demonstration would need to account explicitly for how the functions performed by those steps are supplied within the proposed chemical route.
completion_criteria.label: Chemical route accounts for purification and enzyme-mediated regeneration functions

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries should include independent replication, disclosed concentrations and yields, documented material and energy inputs, and testing across a defined range of sequences and environmental conditions. The number of generations needed to support sustained selection should be justified against carryover, depletion and transient enrichment; the supplied materials provide no established numerical threshold. Finite experiments would establish demonstrated breadth under specified conditions, not literal universality or unlimited evolutionary potential.
completion_criteria.label: Independent replication with disclosed inputs, yields and tested boundaries

completion_criteria.text: Proposed historical boundary: a reproducible laboratory route would satisfy a feasibility claim only within its demonstrated conditions. Claims that the route occurred on early Earth would require additional evidence connecting those conditions, feedstocks and processes to relevant environments and times.
completion_criteria.label: Historical claims connect demonstrated chemistry to early Earth environments

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: BCH-03, “A self-maintaining, evolvable cell assembled from defined components,” shares the goal of sustained evolution but centers on cellular organization and self-maintenance. BCH-04 centers on the chemical emergence of heredity from plausible feedstocks and need not initially produce a cell. Neither achievement would automatically establish the other.

Roster-based comparison: BCH-07, “Autonomous heredity in a chemically distinct genetic polymer,” overlaps directly in copying, fidelity and inherited variation. Its defining distinction is the genetic polymer's chemical identity and autonomous heredity. BCH-04 instead requires a plausible chemical route from feedstocks into evolution; that route could involve RNA or another polymer, but a distinct polymer alone would not satisfy it.

Roster-based comparison: BCH-01, “General design of enzymes for new chemical reactions,” and BCH-02, “Predict biochemical function from molecular sequence and environment,” could contribute catalysts or predictive understanding useful for investigating a route to heredity. Their targets are design and prediction. Successful designed catalysts or accurate predictions would not by themselves demonstrate spontaneous chemical production, reproduction and selection under BCH-04's proposed constraints.

Roster-based comparison: BCH-09, “Predict and control the biochemical organization of condensates,” could intersect with questions of concentration and molecular organization in a proposed route. BCH-10, “Predict modification-dependent biochemical networks,” could intersect with understanding how chemical changes alter interacting molecular processes. Both concern distinct organizational or predictive capabilities; neither requires demonstrating an origin of evolving heredity.

Roster-based comparison: BCH-05, “Routine, comprehensive single-cell proteoform reading,” BCH-06, “A multiplexed biochemical flight recorder for living cells,” and BCH-11, “Routine structural reading of complex glycans,” are measurement capabilities that might inform particular experimental systems. Their subjects and completion targets remain distinct from producing an evolving molecular population from simple feedstocks. BCH-08, “Resolve the nitrogenase reaction cycle during nitrogen fixation,” concerns the mechanism of a specific enzyme system; any connection to feedstock chemistry would depend on a particular proposed route and is not established by the supplied evidence.

unresolved_issues: Substantive Attwater source text remains unavailable in the supplied package. The reported 2025 replication, fragment-copying result and experimental limitations require verification.

The review recommended restoring Attwater details after inspecting substantive text. No inspection was authorized here; the details are therefore retained only as attributed, unverified research reports.
The package does not substantiate feedstock formation or compatibility of the entire proposed chemical chain, and does not determine whether another approach has achieved the integration.
The latest field status as of 1 November 2026 remains unassessed because the supplied search record is empty.
Geochemical defensibility, permitted initial seeds and interventions, sufficient generations, and acceptable dependence on externally supplied catalysts need operational definitions.
The reviewed 2024 article's linked supplementary materials and figure images were not inspected.
No supplied evidence establishes that a laboratory route to evolving heredity occurred historically on early Earth.

brief.title: A route from simple chemicals to evolving molecules
possible: Scientists could start with simple chemicals and build a system whose molecules reproduce, pass on changes and evolve across generations. This would let them test a possible route from nonliving chemistry to heredity—the passing of information from one generation to the next.
why: Connecting chemical production to heredity would help explain how useful molecular information can survive and accumulate. Researchers could compare chemical routes and test how environmental cycles help evolving populations gain complexity.

sources.showed: RNA is a molecule that can carry information and speed chemical reactions. Using supplied short RNA building blocks, an engineered RNA copying molecule and cycles of acidity, freezing and thawing, the team sustained repeated copying, including a fragment of the copying molecule itself.
sources.quote: When combined with coupled pH and freeze–thaw cycles, this enabled exponential replication of both (+) and (−) strands of double-stranded RNAs, including a fragment of the ribozyme itself.
sources.cited_for: Chemical cycles and short building blocks can keep copied RNA strands available for further copying.
sources.not_established: The experiment did not produce its copying molecule and building blocks from simple starting chemicals.

sources.who: Nikolaos Papastavrou, David P. Horning and Gerald F. Joyce
sources.showed: An engineered RNA copying molecule supported reproduction and evolution of a separate RNA that cuts RNA. Variants became better at reproducing while retaining cutting activity.
sources.quote: The increase in fitness was attributable to specific mutations that improved the replicability of the hammerhead, counterbalanced by a small decrease in hammerhead activity.
sources.cited_for: Accurate RNA copying can preserve inherited function while beneficial changes accumulate.
sources.not_established: The copying machinery did not reproduce and evolve independently, and propagation relied on purification and biological enzymes.

shown: Researchers have demonstrated separate pieces of the route: Attwater and colleagues sustained RNA copying through environmental cycles, while Papastavrou and colleagues maintained an evolving functional RNA population. Neither demonstration connected simple starting chemicals to sustained heredity.
missing: A connected chemical route must make information-bearing molecules from plausible starting materials and keep them reproducing under compatible conditions.
The system must supply the functions now performed by repeated laboratory purification and enzyme-assisted regeneration.
Copying must remain accurate enough to preserve useful information as evolving molecules become more complex.

milestones.label: Simple starting chemicals yield molecules that reproduce and undergo selection
milestones.explanation: A system would have to turn geologically plausible starting chemicals into molecules that repeatedly reproduce and undergo selection. This would connect chemical production to evolution.

milestones.label: Sequence changes produce inherited differences in function
milestones.explanation: Changes in the order of molecular building blocks would have to cause functional differences inherited across generations. This would distinguish evolution from persistence or temporary enrichment.

milestones.label: The chemical route sustains regeneration
milestones.explanation: The route would have to provide the functions performed by laboratory purification and enzyme-assisted regeneration. This would explain how usable molecules remain available for continued reproduction.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce the result within tested limits
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce the system with disclosed inputs and yields across defined sequences and conditions. This would establish its reliability and the breadth of sustained selection.

milestones.label: Historical claims connect the chemistry to early Earth
milestones.explanation: A claim that the route occurred on early Earth would need evidence linking its chemicals and conditions to relevant environments and times. This would connect laboratory feasibility to planetary history.

uncertain: Which starting chemicals, initial catalysts and environmental cycles can work together remains open.
How many generations establish sustained selection, rather than temporary enrichment or carryover, needs a justified criterion.
How much external support is acceptable must be defined, including whether the copying machinery must itself reproduce and evolve.

page.title: Prebiotic emergence of Darwinian evolution
page.definition: A laboratory chemical route converts small molecules available before life into a population that reproduces, inherits sequence changes and undergoes natural selection. Its genetic polymers and copying machinery arise through the route under conditions compatible with the proposed planetary environment.

goal.need: In the 2024 RNA experiment, 89.1% copying fidelity per nucleotide over a complete replication cycle supported the evolution of functional RNA. The copying catalyst was supplied rather than reproduced by the evolving population. Connecting synthesis to such inheritance would test how functional information can persist and evolve in chemistry assembled without existing organisms.

figures.caption: Lengths of the copied region and supplied catalyst in the 2024 RNA evolution experiment.
figures.note: These are components of one engineered system, not minimum lengths required for heredity.

statements.quote: Establish replicating, catalytic systems capable of evolution and construct laboratory models of metabolism in primitive living systems.

statements.body: National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine, planetary science and astrobiology decadal survey
statements.quote: Identify and characterize chemical processes and pathways that could enable the transition from abiotic reaction networks to biochemical reaction networks
statements.context: A research priority under Strategic Research for Q9.1.

statements.quote: A comprehensive understanding of the mechanisms necessary for the emergence of life requires an examination of how all of these components can evolve as a single integrated system.
statements.context: The components are small-molecule reaction networks, functional and information polymers, and selectively permeable compartments.

completion.title: A connected prebiotic chemical route produces a self-sustaining population undergoing Darwinian evolution.
completion.criterion: Demonstrate one connected laboratory route from specified small-molecule feedstocks and energy sources to a self-sustaining chemical population exhibiting reproduction, heritable variation and differential reproductive success. Feedstocks, catalysts and environmental transitions must be supported by a specified prebiotic setting. Genetic polymers and their copying machinery must originate through the route, rather than enter as engineered seeds or be regenerated by external biological enzymes. Continued supply of feedstocks and energy is permitted. No fixed yield, fidelity or generation count is imposed.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis of NASA's prebiotic-chemistry objectives and the origins-of-life working definition; no external operational test for their integration was found.
completion.basis: Searches of NASA's 1998 and 2003 roadmaps, Ames Objective 7.1, the National Academies' decadal strategy, and origins-of-life challenge and prize documents found no integrated test specifying allowed seeds, interventions and duration. This criterion joins the published goals of chemistry constrained by prebiotic environments and self-sustaining Darwinian evolution.

milestones.title: Laboratory chemistry produces organic compounds under simulated primordial planetary conditions.
milestones.criterion: Produce organic compounds in laboratory simulations of specified primordial planetary conditions; NASA sets no minimum yield. Powner, Gerland and Sutherland, published on 14 May 2009, synthesized activated pyrimidine ribonucleotides from cyanamide, cyanoacetylene, glycolaldehyde, glyceraldehyde and inorganic phosphate. This demonstrates building-block chemistry rather than a reproducing system.
milestones.set_by: NASA, 2003 Astrobiology Roadmap, Objective 3.1, example investigations.
milestones.threshold_quote: Identify the organic compounds and complexes produced under primordial planetary conditions through laboratory simulation experiments.

milestones.title: Chemical pathways produce genetic polymers under early-Earth environmental constraints.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate chemical pathways to genetic polymers consistent with early-Earth thermodynamic and environmental constraints. Ferris and colleagues, published on 2 May 1996, elongated a supplied synthetic 10-unit primer to chains exceeding 50 units after 14 daily additions of activated adenosine monomers on montmorillonite clay at 25 °C. The supplied primer and activated monomers leave their prebiotic production outside this demonstration. An independent replicate count is not given for this elongation series.
milestones.set_by: NASA, 1998 Astrobiology Roadmap, Objective 2, implementation; genetic polymers are the nucleic-acid component of this broader objective.
milestones.threshold_quote: Conduct ground-based laboratory research on chemical pathways leading to the emergence of the macromolecules of life. These pathways should be consistent with the thermodynamic and environmental constraints on the early earth.

milestones.title: A molecular chemical system sustains repeated replication.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate repeated molecular replication in a laboratory chemical system; NASA specifies no cycle count. Attwater and colleagues, published on 28 May 2025, reported exponential amplification of both strands of a cloned RNA duplex over four cycles, with three independent reactions per cycle. Separate experiments ran for 21 cycles with five serial dilutions. The system received supplied polymerase ribozyme, primers and activated trinucleotides; dilution replenished catalyst and substrates.
milestones.threshold_quote: Through laboratory experiments, develop and characterize self-replicating systems based on diverse molecules and recognition mechanisms.

milestones.title: Artificial chemical populations undergo mutation and natural selection.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate mutation and selection acting on reproducing chemical populations. Papastavrou, Horning and Joyce, published on 4 March 2024, ran two RNA lineages for eight rounds. Five evolved hammerhead variants showed three- to eightfold higher calculated fitness than the starting sequence; biochemical assays used three replicates. Gel purification, reverse transcription, PCR and transcription regenerated the population between rounds.
milestones.threshold_quote: Without regard to how life actually emerged on Earth, create and study artificial chemical systems that undergo mutation and natural selection in the laboratory.

milestones.title: A chemical population sustains Darwinian evolution while maintaining its own copying machinery.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate reproduction, inherited variation and selection while the population maintains its copying machinery. Preassembled genetic polymers, activated building blocks and energy inputs are permitted. No universal generation count is specified. Gianni and colleagues, published on 12 February 2026, showed separate QT45-catalyzed syntheses of its complement and itself, yielding 0.24% and 0.17% after 72 days at −7 °C; self-synthesis required a supplied six-nucleotide substrate. Replicate counts for these yields are not stated in the main text. The authors state that self-sustained replication remains unachieved.
milestones.set_by: Origins-of-life working convention described by Gerald Joyce in the Institute of Medicine's 2011 workshop summary, pages 24–26; autonomous RNA evolution is also an explicit criterion in Papastavrou and colleagues' 2024 paper.
milestones.threshold_quote: a self-sustained chemical system capable of undergoing Darwinian evolution.

not_found: No external operational protocol for the complete feedstock-to-evolution route was found.
No universal minimum yield, copying fidelity or generation count for evolving prebiotic heredity was found.
No report demonstrating the complete connected route was found.

results.finding: A cloned RNA duplex underwent exponential replication over four cycles, with three independent reactions per cycle.
results.detail: The system used supplied polymerase ribozyme, primers and activated trinucleotides. A separate experiment continued for 21 cycles with serial dilution and replenishment.

results.finding: Shorter RNA products in a random-sequence replication experiment increased up to 30-fold; the replicate count was not stated.
results.detail: The changing population bears on differential amplification, but the text does not establish mutation and natural selection acting on inherited variants.
results.quote: These persisted and increased up to 30-fold in abundance.

results.finding: A ribozyme replicated a 29-nucleotide fragment of its own sequence, with three independent reactions per cycle.
results.detail: Fragmentary self-replication did not maintain the complete copying machinery; fresh ribozyme was supplied during dilution.
results.quote: These results show that (1) a ribozyme can exponentially replicate part of itself from short building blocks, (2) this ‘fragmentary’ self-replication can occur in a ‘one-pot’ cycled reaction and (3) ribozymes can initiate replication on themselves, even in the absence of a seed template.

results.finding: Two RNA lineages underwent eight rounds of replication and selection.
results.detail: Each round included RNA-catalyzed synthesis of both strands. Reverse transcription, PCR and transcription regenerated the population between rounds.
results.quote: This process was continued for eight rounds for each lineage, after which materials from each round were analyzed by deep sequencing to determine the course of hammerhead evolution.

results.finding: Five evolved hammerhead variants had three- to eightfold higher calculated fitness than the starting RNA.
results.detail: Two lineages were evolved; biochemical fitness measurements used three replicates. The population was regenerated between rounds using reverse transcription, PCR and transcription.
results.quote: The net effect, multiplying the yields from plus- and minus-strand synthesis and the requisite RNA-cleavage activity of the plus strand, is that the evolved variants have an overall three- to eightfold improvement in fitness compared to Seq0 ( Fig. 4 B ).

results.finding: Prebiotic synthesis produced 2-amino-oxazole in 75% isolated yield; sample size not reported.
results.detail: The study also synthesized activated pyrimidine ribonucleotides from plausible prebiotic feedstocks under conditions consistent with potential early-Earth geochemical models. It demonstrates building-block chemistry, not a reproducing system.
results.quote:
1H NMR analysis revealed
that 2-amino-oxazole 11 was produced in .80% yield (75% isolated
yield) (Fig. 2c).

results.finding: Prebiotic laboratory chemistry produced precursors of 3 classes of biomolecules; sample size not reported.
results.detail: Experiments used prebiotically plausible intermediates, UV light and hydrogen sulfide. The proposed Hadean Earth setting is a geochemical scenario; the complete reaction network was not demonstrated in one pot.
results.quote: We show that precursors of ribonucleotides, amino acids and lipids can all be derived by reductive homologation of hydrogen cyanide and some of its derivatives and thus that all the cellular subsystems could have arisen simultaneously through common chemistry.

results.finding: Prebiotic one-pot synthesis produced phosphorylated nucleosides at 19% yield relative to cytidine; sample size not reported.
results.detail: The experiment used a phosphate-containing mineral and evaporation at 85°C, simulating wet-dry conditions proposed for early Earth. It produced RNA building blocks, not a reproducing system.
results.quote:
LC-MS analysis of the reaction now showed formation of phosphorylated 
nucleosides (Fig. 3A) in remarkable 19% yield relative to cytidine (Fig. 3B and Fig. S7).

results.finding: Wet–dry cycling of four cyclic nucleotides produced RNA oligomers up to 10 units long; 2 independent replicates.
results.detail: At room temperature, alkaline wet–dry cycles produced mixed-base oligomers without external activators. The cyclic nucleotide starting materials were purchased; their prebiotic production was not demonstrated in this experiment.
results.quote:
This leads to
a broad distribution of A, U, G, and C mixed sequence oligomers, up
to 6% of 4-mer and 0.1% of 10-mer, paving the way for RNA replication
and evolution through subsequent templated ligation under the same
pH.

results.finding: Basalt-glass RNA oligomerization: sample size not stated; longest products interpreted as >100 nucleotides.
results.detail: Borate did not inhibit oligomerization of supplied uridine triphosphate on basaltic glass after three weeks. The experiment did not demonstrate an integrated pathway from simple precursors to the polymers; the longest lengths were inferred from gel electrophoresis.
results.quote: The longest are interpreted as being >100 nts.

results.finding: A pair of cross-replicating RNA enzymes sustained replication through 50 successive transfers; independent replicate count not reported.
results.detail: Each transfer replenished four oligonucleotide substrates. No enzymes were added after the initial reaction except those carried over from the preceding mixture.
results.quote:
This process was repeated for 50 successive transfers as the replicating molecules withstood an overall dilution of 10
100
-fold (
Figure 6B
).

results.finding: Across three RNA evolution experiments, reproducing populations diversified; the main experiment ended with five coexisting RNA lineages.
results.detail: Sequencing identified mutations and changing lineage frequencies. Replication used a reconstituted E. coli translation system and serial transfers in water-in-oil droplets. The two additional experiments began from an intermediate population in the main experiment.
results.quote: The final population, comprising five RNA lineages, forms a replicator network with diverse interactions, including cooperation to help the replication of all other members.

results.finding: In two self-replicating molecular systems, natural selection favored mutants that catalyzed production of their own replication precursors.
results.detail: Selection depended on mutants activating a photocatalyst that produced singlet oxygen, accelerating formation of replicator precursors.
results.quote: Here we show the emergence of Darwinian evolution in two systems of self-replicating molecules in which natural selection favours replicator mutants best capable of catalysing the production of the precursors required for their own replication.

results.finding: Cross-replicating RNA enzymes: among 100 sequenced clones, the three most abundant recombinants accounted for one third.
results.detail: Over 20 serial reactions, the RNA enzymes cross-replicated using supplied oligonucleotide substrates. Recombinant sequences could cross-replicate, and competition favored variants with greater fitness in the substrate mixture.
results.quote:
The three most abundant recombinants
were A5B2, A5B3, and A5B4 (and their cross-
replication partners), which together accounted for
one third of all clones.
